properties.description: Name of the laboratory or institution hosting the instrument.
Persistent identifier for the laboratory (e.g., ROR ID).

Identifier for the analytical session this record describes — the laboratory's own run, sequence or batch identifier as generated by the instrument or acquisition software. Distinct from any persistent identifier a repository mints on submission.
Date on which the analytical session began. For sessions spanning multiple days, use the date of the first session. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.
Date on which the analytical session ended. May equal Analysis Start Date for single-day sessions. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

Name or identifier of each sample analysed in this session, as used in the laboratory — a sample mount, section or aliquot counts as one entry where that is what the laboratory tracks. Should match the identifier used in associated publications or data tables.

Globally unique, persistent identifier for each sample listed in Sample Name. IGSN (International Geo Sample Number) is the recommended standard for geological and cosmochemical samples, as used by Astromat, EarthChem and SESAR. Where a sample and its sub-samples are separately registered, record the identifier at the level actually analysed.

Instrument control, automation and data acquisition software used to collect the raw data, including version number. Distinct from Data Processing Software(s), which covers everything applied to the data after acquisition.

Any procedure- or analysis-specific information not captured by a structured field anywhere in this TAPP — including anomalies, deviations from the registered procedure, instrument modifications, and supplementary context. Scope is the whole document, not Group 6: this is the last field of the TAPP and covers all six groups. Use sparingly; a structured field is preferred for anything that can be formally categorised.

The form in which the sample is presented to the instrument, and the preparation that brought it to that form — for example mounting, sectioning, polishing, coating, crushing, fusion, or extraction of an electron-transparent section. Record 'None' where the material is analysed as received.

DOI or unique persistent identifier for the registered procedure used in this analysis, generated upon procedure submission to a data repository. If a DOI has been applied for but not yet minted, enter "pending".
Name(s) of the analyst(s) who performed the analysis session. ORCID is recommended for persistent identification.

Grants and other funding sources that supported the specific sample analyses and data collection reported here. Include grant numbers and funding agencies. Distinct from procedure development funding, which may have been awarded years earlier.

DOI or other persistent identifier for the co-registered dataset or publication where both datasets are reported together. Accepts: a dedicated dataset DOI (if separately deposited), a shared dataset DOI (if co-submitted in the same package), or a publication DOI. Use "same submission" if the coupled dataset is included in this data package, or "pending" if not yet assigned. If coupling is documented through a shared sample identifier only, that information is already captured in Sample Persistent Identifier (Group 2).

Other analytical techniques applied to the same sample(s) whose results are intended to be interpreted together with data from this procedure. Document coupling with any technique whose results are functionally linked to this dataset — providing calibration inputs, complementary spatial context, or required companion measurements. Name the instrument, laboratory or purpose alongside each technique where known, and join multiple techniques with '; '. Enter "None" if no coupling is intended.

Description of how this procedure is coupled with the technique(s) listed above. Include: (1) the functional relationship — what data or context flows between techniques, or how results are combined (e.g. which output from the coupled technique serves as input to data reduction for this technique); and (2) the analytical sequence — which technique is performed first and why (e.g. non-destructive before destructive). Required when Coupled Technique(s) is not "None".

Registered procedure DOI for the coupled technique named above. If the coupled procedure has not yet been registered, enter the DOI of a publication describing the coupled method, or "pending". Enter "None" if no coupling is planned.
Domain-specific type classifications. Should include a scientific instrument type URI (e.g. wd:Q3099911 for Wikidata scientific instrument).
Human-readable name for this instrument.
Text description of this instrument, its purpose, and capabilities.
Alternate name(s), e.g. specific make/model designation, common abbreviation.
Formal identifier(s) for this instrument. Use PropertyValue for structured identifiers (e.g. PIDINST, serial number, inventory number).
Landing page URL for this instrument.
Organization that manufactured this instrument.
Product model information for this instrument.
Model name or number.
Model identifier.
Instrument type classification(s) from a controlled vocabulary.
Organization that owns this instrument.
Agents associated with this instrument in specific roles (e.g. operator, custodian, principal investigator). Use schema:owner for the owning organization.

Instrument-specific properties (measured variables, detection limits, calibration information, operating parameters, etc.). On a procedure / plan instrument (e.g. an instrument named directly on an ada:TAPPDefinition) these are schema:PropertyValueSpecification parameter templates (an overridable default); on a prov:used analysis-event instrument they are schema:PropertyValue concrete values. The JSON Schema accepts both; a profile SHACL rule pins which form applies in which context.
Date the instrument was commissioned (ISO 8601).
Date the instrument was decommissioned (ISO 8601). Absent if still operational.
Sub-components of this instrument system. Each item is either an inline instrument description or an @id reference.
Links to related resources (manuals, datasheets, calibration records, related instruments).
Role of the related resource as a SKOS Concept (DCAT canonical role slot).
URI of the related resource (DCAT canonical pointer to what is being related to; distinct from schema:url which is the presentation URL inherited from labeledLink).
Catalog record metadata-about-metadata for this instrument description.
Date this metadata record was last modified (ISO 8601).
Schema or profile this metadata record conforms to.
Shape and dimensions of the laser ablation spot in micrometres registered by the procedure. For circular spots, report diameter; for square or rectangular spots, report width × length.

Laser pulse energy per unit area at the sample surface in J cm⁻², as registered by the procedure. If the system reports only as % of maximum output, include that value and note the system maximum where known.
Laser pulse repetition rate in hertz registered by the procedure.

Total on-sample ablation (signal acquisition) time per individual spot in seconds, as set in the acquisition method. For transect analysis, the equivalent procedure-level parameter is scan speed (captured in Transect Rate, Mapping Rate or Step Size). For mapping analysis, total acquisition time is sample-area-dependent and is not captured here.

Depth of the ablation pit produced under the registered laser conditions, the method used to measure it, and the resulting per-pulse ablation rate. For transect and mapping the equivalent quantity is trench depth under the same conditions.
Distance between adjacent raster lines in a 2D elemental map, measured perpendicular to the scan direction, in micrometres. Applies to raster mapping only.
Diameter of the laser spot as independently measured on the sample or on a test material, distinct from the nominal value the procedure registers.

An externally-calibrated factor that converts the measured quantity into the reported quantity, how it was determined, and its uncertainty. Applies where the conversion depends on a factor calibrated against a reference of independently known value, rather than on the instrument response alone. Distinct from the fields that name the calibration material and that state which approach applies to which analyte, where the technique has them: this field records the resulting factor itself.

The statistic reported to show whether scatter among the contributing analyses exceeds what analytical uncertainty alone predicts, together with its value. The procedure may still state an acceptance threshold, which belongs with the inclusion criteria.
Serial number or laboratory-internal identifier for the specific instrument unit.

Instrument sensitivity achieved in the session, with the isotope or channel it was measured on and the conditions it applies to. May be expressed either as detected signal per unit concentration or per unit mass of analyte delivered — counts per second per ppb, volts per ppm, counts per picogram — or as useful yield, the percentage of sampled atoms ultimately detected as ions, with the method used to derive it cited. A sensitivity the procedure requires before analyses may begin belongs with the tuning acceptance criteria.
Formal identifier (IGSN, catalog number, GeoReM ID).
Registry code for the material on the schema:DefinedTerm path.
The registry the schema:termCode belongs to.

Quality-control reference material(s) measured as unknowns alongside samples to assess accuracy independently and to monitor drift. Give the material name, its source, and a citation for the accepted or reference values used for comparison.

properties.description: The measured level of the analytical blank in the session, and — where the reported quantity is a ratio — its composition, since a blank subtracted from a ratio biases the result unless its own composition is known. Companion to the blank correction method.
Narrower (child) concepts in the hierarchy. Items are inline concept objects or @id references.
Broader (parent) concepts in the hierarchy. Items are inline concept objects or @id references.
Concept scheme(s) this concept belongs to.
General note about this concept.
Formal explanation of the meaning of this concept.
Classification code for this concept within a scheme (a single notation string, consistent with CdifCodelistConcept).
Preferred lexical label for this concept. A single string, a single language-tagged value, or an array of language-tagged values. Each language should appear at most once.
A representative code for this keyword in the controlled vocabulary. Analogous to skos:Notation

The controlled vocabulary responsible for this keyword, as EITHER a plain URI string identifying the vocabulary, OR an object reference ({"@id": "<uri>"}) to a vocabulary defined elsewhere in the document. Both forms are already in use across CDIF profiles and downstream ADA building blocks; permitting only the string form made the object form - the natural JSON-LD spelling of a reference - invalid, while this class's own union-type policy above explicitly anticipates both.
text label for the term that is useful to human user

string label for person that is meaningful for human users, should format consistently. Recommend 'Family Name, Given name' format.
web-resolveable string for the identifier; host name part is location of a resolver that will return some representation for the given identifier value. E.g. https://doi.org/10.5066/F7VX0DMQ
the identifier string. E.g. 10.5066/F7VX0DMQ

In this context for the schema:PropertyValue, this field is an identifier for the identifier schema, e.g. DOI, ARK.  Get values from https://registry.identifiers.org/registry/ for interoperability. URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}) so they participate in RDF entailment; free-label strings remain valid as strings.
identifier or name for the property concept quantified by the values in this variable slot. Multiple values can specify the property at different levels of granularity.
Component type classification.
